# measurement script to time sum(range(1, 10_000_001)) five independent runs
import time
import sys
import platform
import datetime
import statistics

EXPECTED = 50000005000000

measurement_code = '''
from time import perf_counter
s = sum(range(1, 10_000_001))
# one timed run shown; the actual script runs this five times independently
'''

def main():
    times = []
    computed = None
    print('Starting measurement: sum(range(1, 10_000_001))')
    for i in range(1, 6):
        start = time.perf_counter()
        s = sum(range(1, 10_000_001))
        end = time.perf_counter()
        elapsed = end - start
        times.append(elapsed)
        computed = s
        print(f'Run {i}: elapsed={elapsed:.9f} sec, sum={s}')
    py_ver = platform.python_version() + ' (' + sys.version.splitlines()[0] + ')'
    ts = datetime.datetime.now().isoformat()
    print('\nPython version:', py_ver)
    print('Timestamp:', ts)
    print('Expected sum:', EXPECTED)
    print('Verified equal:', computed == EXPECTED)
    print('\nMeasurement code used:')
    print(measurement_code)
    # Print summary
    print('\nSummary statistics:')
    print('times:', times)
    print('mean:', statistics.mean(times))
    print('median:', statistics.median(times))
    print('min:', min(times))
    print('max:', max(times))

if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
